results.title: Decoding decision-making: The interplay of cognitive ...
results.content: This research seeks to answer the critical question: “How do managers’ construal levels influence the performance of their ventures, and what role does working capital management play in this relationship?” In exploring the synergy between CLT and working capital management, our study aims to provide fresh insights into the cognitive underpinnings of financial decision-making in new ventures, offering a new perspective that transcends traditional financial metrics. Building on the arguments presented in Hypotheses 1–3 explores the complex interplay between cognitive strategies (managerial construal level) and financial pressures (working capital management constraint) in shaping a new venture’s performance trajectory. This study represents a pioneering effort to integrate CLT (Trope & Liberman, Citation2010), a concept rooted in cognitive psychology, with the practical challenges of working capital management in new ventures (Aktas et al., Citation2015). Our findings demonstrate that managers’ construal levels significantly shape their approach to managing working capital, thereby affecting the financial stability and growth potential of their ventures (Baños-Caballero et al., Citation2014).
